the 23a.2-3 baraita: the dispute and the maaseh on the ship

props.gloss_en: the mishnah: one who makes his sukkah at the top of a ship -- it is valid (the clause also names the top of a wagon)
the stam: whose is the mishnah? It is R' Akiva's
the baraita: one who makes his sukkah at the top of a ship -- Rabban Gamliel invalidates
the maaseh: Rabban Gamliel and R' Akiva were travelling on a ship; R' Akiva built a sukkah at its top, and the next day a wind blew and uprooted it
Rabban Gamliel said to him: Akiva, where is your sukkah? (rhetorical; what it implies is not stated -- header)
Abaye: all agree that where it cannot withstand a typical land wind, it is nothing
Abaye: where it can withstand an atypical land wind, all agree it is valid
Abaye: where they dispute is a sukkah that withstands a typical land wind but not an atypical land wind
Rabban Gamliel, as Abaye gives him: we require a sukkah that is a permanent dwelling
Rabban Gamliel, as Abaye gives him: since it cannot withstand a typical sea wind, it is nothing
Abaye: Rabban Gamliel's invalidation of the middle case is grounded in the permanent-dwelling requirement
R' Akiva, as Abaye gives him: we require a sukkah that is a temporary dwelling
R' Akiva, as Abaye gives him: since it withstands a typical land wind, it is valid
Abaye: R' Akiva's validation of the middle case is grounded in the temporary-dwelling requirement
